thread:
maria: FYI noticed a ~10-12% p95 decode latency regression on small-batch workloads after the kernel-routing change. posting traces and bench numbers.

kevin: which commit/PR?

maria: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823 — the selector refactor that changed fallback ordering. quick summary: prefilling and decode routing now share more heuristics.

anita: got it. could be the selector now prefers a paged-attn variant for tiny batches. any flamegraphs?

maria: pasted a quick nvprof snippet:
```
GPU: 2 x kernels: flash_attn_fused_v2_launch (~38%), paged_attn_apply_kv (~26%), kv_cache_eviction_worker (~12%), memcpy H2D (~8%)
user: p95 decode 124ms -> 140ms after change (batch 2, seq 16)
```

perf-bot: nightly smallbatch bench (canary): baseline p95=120ms, canary p95=138ms, qps down ~6%. Full output uploaded to /bench/2026-03-15/small-decode.json

tom: hypothesis: continuous batching distribution shifted; more microbatches with shape (b=2,s=16) are now routed to paged path because the selector weights seq thresholds differently. paged path has extra KV page handling that kills small-batch latency.

kevin: I inspected selector code: selector/heuristics.go lines ~180. logic: if batch_size <= 4 AND seq_len <= 32 choose fused, otherwise paged. BUT the refactor introduced a name mapping bug: fused variant renamed to "flash_attn_fused_v2_launch" and the mapping expects "flash_attn_fused". so it doesn't match, falls back to paged.

anita: that would explain the kernel landing. Also eviction counts in the trace look suspicious (kv_cache_eviction_worker). maybe the paged variant triggers extra cache churn because of page alignment differences.

maria: quick repro command I used:
```
./bench_small_decode --model=gpt2 --batch=2 --seq=16 --workload=decode --runs=500
```
Result: with selector=canary (new code) p95=140ms, with selector=reverted p95=119ms.

kevin: proposed fix: add explicit alias mapping for fused_v2 in selector and incrementally prefer fused variants for batch<=4, seq<=48. also add a guard that records kernel_name chosen per request to metrics so we can correlate.

maria: I implemented a quick patch: selector: add alias and change seq threshold to 48 for decode. also Instrumentation: metric label infer.kernel_name. pushed in PR 4830 and canary deployed.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-3214: "selector aliasing -> fused_v2 miss causes paged fallback and small-batch p95 regression". Link: https://tracker.redwood.ai/INF-3214

perf-bot: re-ran microbench on canary after patch: p95=122ms, qps back within 1% of baseline.

anita: nice. follow-ups: 1) add unit test for kernel name aliasing, 2) write a microtrace that counts page hits/evictions per-kernel, 3) consider default selector fallback ordering explicitly documented.

kevin: agree on unit test and metric. I'll open a follow-up PR to add the microtrace hook.

maria: thanks all. I'll leave the canary up and monitor metrics for 24h. created a short runbook in the PR about rolling back if q95 climbs.

tom: :thumbsup: 

maria: tagging @oncall in case we see any spike.

kevin: sounds good, will watch dashboards.

maria: end.
